{{short description|German mathematician (born 1967)}}
[[File:Prof. Dr. Peter Benner.jpg|thumb]]
'''Peter Benner''' (born May 25, 1967) is a German mathematician specialized in dynamical systems and [[numerical analysis]]. He was managing director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems]] in [[Magdeburg, Germany]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Forschungsportal Sachsen-Anhalt |url=https://forschung-sachsen-anhalt.de/pl/benner-117218 |website=forschung-sachsen-anhalt.de |language=de |date=11 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Wie das Max-Planck-Institut Magdeburg stärken möchte |url=https://www.volksstimme.de/lokal/magdeburg/wie-das-max-planck-institut-magdeburg-starken-mochte-3336023 |website=www.volksstimme.de |language=de}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Benner was born in [[Kirchen (Sieg)]]. After graduating from high school in 1986 at the Freiherr vom Stein Gymnasium in Betzdorf, Benner studied mathematics with a minor in economics/operations research at the [[RWTH Aachen University]] from 1987. In 1993 he received the Springorum commemorative coin from RWTH Aachen for his diploma thesis. He received his doctorate in 1997 in the field of mathematics from the [[Chemnitz University of Technology]] under the supervision of [[Volker Mehrmann]]. From 1997 to 2001 he worked as a research assistant at the Center for Technomathematics at the [[University of Bremen]]. He completed his habilitation there in 2001.<ref name=ovgu></ref>

From 2001 to 2003, Benner taught as a senior assistant at the Institute for Mathematics at [[Technische Universität Berlin]]. In the meantime he worked as a visiting professor at the [[Hamburg University of Technology]]. In 2003 he accepted a professorship for mathematics in industry and technology at [[Chemnitz University of Technology]]. Benner was a visiting scientist and professor at the [[University of Kansas]], the [[Università di Modena e Reggio Emilia]], the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of [[New York University]], Virginia Tech, the [[Université du Littoral Côte d'Opale]] in Calais and Shanghai University employed. In 2018 he was a [[J. Tinsley Oden]] Faculty Fellow at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=ovgu>{{cite web |title=Peter Benner |url=https://www.smartprosys.ovgu.de/symposium2022speaker_benner.html |website=smartprosys |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Peter Benner übernimmt Amt des Geschäftsführenden Direktors |url=https://idw-online.de/de/news514361 |website=idw-online.de}}</ref>

In 2010, Benner was appointed director and scientific member at the [[Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Chemnitzer Mathematiker ist neuer MPI-Direktor |url=https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/tu/pressestelle/aktuell/3305 |website=www.tu-chemnitz.de |language=de |date=22 December 2023}}</ref> He began research there with his specialist group Computational Methods in Systems and Control Theory at the Max Planck Institute on May 1, 2010. In the same year he was a visiting professor at the Université du Littoral Côte d'Opale in Calais, France. At the beginning of 2011 he was appointed honorary professor of mathematics at the [[Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg]]. In 2015, he was Distinguished Professor at Shanghai University. Since 2017 he has been a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) since 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Peter Benner |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37267033500 |website=[[IEEE]]}}</ref>

Benner is co-editor of various publications and mathematical journals, including the SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications and co-author of various software packages. He is involved in mathematical societies, including SIAM and the Society for Applied Mathematics and Mechanics (GAMM). He has also been a member of the Niconet e.V. association since 2006. V., who develops and maintains the software library “Subroutine Library in Systems and Control” (SLICOT).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Benner |first1=Peter |last2=Mehrmann |first2=Volker |last3=Sima |first3=Vasile |last4=Van Huffel |first4=Sabine |last5=Varga |first5=Andras |chapter=SLICOT—A Subroutine Library in Systems and Control Theory |title=Applied and Computational Control, Signals, and Circuits |date=1999 |pages=499–539 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-0571-5_10|isbn=978-1-4612-6822-2 |chapter-url=https://elib.dlr.de/28549/1/varga_nic97-3.pdf }}</ref>
